protocol.assessment: Classify burn degree: First-degree (red, painful, no blisters — superficial). Second-degree (blisters, swelling, severe pain — partial thickness). Third-degree (white/charred, leathery, may be painless — full thickness). Estimate total body surface area (TBSA) affected using the Rule of Nines. Assess airway for inhalation injury (singed facial hair, soot in mouth, hoarse voice).
steps: 1. Ensure the scene is safe and remove the patient from the source of the burn.
2. Call emergency services (911) for burns larger than the patient's palm, burns to the face, hands, feet, genitals, joints, or circumferential burns.
3. Cool the burn immediately with cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 10-20 minutes.
4. Remove clothing and jewelry near the burned area before swelling begins, unless adhered to the skin.
5. After cooling, cover the burn loosely with a sterile, non-adhesive dressing or clean cling film.
6. For chemical burns, brush off dry chemicals first, then flush continuously with large amounts of water for at least 20 minutes.
7. For electrical burns, do not touch the patient until the power source is disconnected; assess for cardiac arrhythmias and entry/exit wounds.
8. Monitor for shock, keep the patient warm (cover unburned areas), and provide small sips of water if the patient is conscious and alert.
do_not: Do NOT apply ice, butter, toothpaste, or any home remedies to the burn.
Do NOT burst blisters, as they protect the underlying tissue from infection.
Do NOT remove clothing or material stuck to the burned skin.
Do NOT use fluffy cotton or adhesive bandages directly on the burn.
protocol.when_to_escalate: Escalate immediately for third-degree burns of any size, second-degree burns larger than 10% TBSA, burns involving the face/airway/hands/feet/genitals/joints, electrical or chemical burns, burns in children under 5 or adults over 60, or when signs of inhalation injury are present.
